DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Building, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG Legal Opinion No. 48 S. 2015 PB CLEMENTE U. FELIX, JR. 1 1 DEC 2015 SBM MANOLO A. CAYETANO Barangay Bayan-Bayanan, Malabon City Dear Gentlemen: This refers to your respective letters concerning the issue on who is the rightful applicant for a fidelity bond with the Bureau of Treasury (BTr) based on the facts as culled from your respective letters: A criminal charge was filed against Punong Barangay (PB) Clemente U. Felix (hereinafter, "PB Clemente"), which is currently pending before the Regional Trial Court (RTC) of Malabon City. Prior to PB Clemente's posting of bail, the highest ranking Sangguniang Barangay Member (SBM), Manolo A. Cayetano (hereinafter, "SBM Cayetano"), was appointed on 01 July 2015 as Acting PB. Consequently, SBM Cayetano applied for fidelity bond and was issued the same by the BTr during his assumption as Acting P B. On 08 October 2015, PB Clemente informed DILG-Malabon City that he has posted bail and is now ready to assume his duties and responsibilities effective 09 October 2015. Thereafter, on 13 October 2015 DILG-Malabon City issued a certification stating that PB Clemente has assumed his duties and responsibilities as PB effective 09 October 2015. On 12 October 2015, the SB of Bayan-bayanan issued Kapasiyahang Pambarangay IO-02- 15 designating SBM Gregorio G. Felix (hereinafter, "SBM Gregorio") and Barangay Treasurer Levitica F. Flores as official signatory for all barangay transactions with Landbank Malabon City. On 14 October 2015, PB Clemente appointed SBM Gregorio as Finance Officer of the barangay effective immediately subject to the general supervision of the former. On similar date, the SB of Bayan-bayan issued Resolution No. 10-15-2015 approving the appointment of SBM Gregorio as Finance Officer of the barangay for the year 2015. On 28 October 2015, SBM Cayetano requested this Department's intervention as it is his opinion that SBM Gregorio has no authority to post a fidelity bond on the basis of Section 46 (a), Local Government Code (LGC), which provides that the highest ranking SBM shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the PB in case

of the latter's temporary incapacity to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons. He asserts that as the highest ranking SBM, he shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the PB in view of PB Clemente's incapacity to disburse funds due to the pending cases filed against him. This includes the responsibility to post the fidelity bond, approve vouchers and payrolls, and countersign checks in accordance with Sections 344 and 345 of the LGC. Thus, in his opinion, the resolution issued by the SB is ultra vires, and the posting of fidelity bond by SBM Gregorio is bereft of legal basis. On 29 October 2015, PB Clemente wrote DILG-Malabon City requesting for a certification in compliance with the 26 October 2015 letter of COA-Malabon City (hereinafter, the "COA") requesting a copy of a certification from the Director Of DILG- Malabon City showing that the status of PB Clemente as PB of Bayan-Bayan remains. The said COA letter was in response to the 20 October 2015 letter of SBM Gregorio inquiring whether he may sign the Punong Barangay Certification (PBC) in his capacity as the official bonded by the BTr for reason that the bond of PB Clemente was not renewed by the BTr in view of a pending criminal case filed against the latter before the RTC of Malabon City. In said letter, the COA interposed no objection on the barangay's designated Finance Officer as signatory to the P BC on the basis of Sections 2.11 and 2.32 of COA Circular No. 2012-005 subject to the submission of the above certification. On 02 November 2015, the COA, in response to a 28 October 2015 letter of SBM Cayetano requesting for the cancellation of the fidelity bond issued in favor of SBM Gregorio, informed SBM Cayetano that they requested the officials of the barangay to clarify the matter with this Department as well as secure the necessary certification to thresh out the issue of who is currently the acting PB of Bayan-Bayanan. In addition, the COA informed SBM Cayetano of its letter to SBM Gregorio, on even date, requesting for the submission of a copy of the Barangay's Internal Rules of Procedures pursuant to Section 50, LGC to purposely document the appointment of SBM Gregorio as the appointed Finance Officer of that Barangay. Hence, this request. This Department shall limit its discussion on matters within its mandate and competence, specifically the interpretation of the pertinent provisions of the LGC in relation to the issue at hand. 2.1. 2.3. The responsibility to initiate, process, approved financial transactions and issue a Punong Barangay's Certification ("BC) under oath to government (barangay) depository banks to honor/encash checks issued shall be the responsibility of the barangay officials. The PB shall issue the PBC under oath to the depository bank for checks issued by the barangay only after he has duly examined and been satisfied that the (a) the DVS are duly certified by the proper barangay officials and approved by the PB; (b) the expenditure or disbursement is proper and valid; and (c) the SDS are complete. With the submission of the PBC to the authorized government depository bank (AGDB), the PB shall be primarily accountable for all losses arising from its issuance.

Termina tion of Tem ra Inca acit In DILG Opinion No. 25, s. 2002, we opined that a PB who has a pending criminal case and presently out on bail can still continue to perform his duties and functions considering that under Section 46(a)3, LGC, pendency of a criminal charge is not among the grounds for temporary incapacity due to physical or legal reasons that renders the PB temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties and functions. In the case of PB Clemente, his temporary incapacity terminated upon his posting of bail in addition to his actual resumption of duties. Application for Fidelity Disbursement of Fund' Disqualification Bond: LCE's Anent the issue on who is the rightful applicant for fidelity bond for purposes of LGU fund disbursement (considering PB Clemente's disqualification to post fidelity bond with the BTr due to the pending case against him), note that the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member's exercise of the powers and performance of the duties and functions of the PB ceased/terminated upon resumption of duties by the latter. Section 46, LGC, does not make any distinction as to termination of incapacity. Hence, the PB's capacity/incapacity cannot be qualified such that he is considered to be capacitated in the performance of other powers and functions, with exception to the disbursement of funds. As such, SBM Cayetano cannot insist on assuming part of the powers and duties of PB Clemente on account of the latter's disqualification to apply for fidelity bond. This now raises the issue on whether the application for fidelity bond may be designated by PB Clemente considering his disqualification to apply for the same on account of the BTr's requirement/qualification that the applicant should not have a pending criminal case against him. We note that under Section 3444, LGC, the approval of the disbursement voucher by the local chief executive himself is required whenever local funds are disbursed." In 3 Section 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. - (a) When the governor, city or municipal mayor, or punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-governor, city or municipal vice- mayor, or the highest ranking Sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period Of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. Section 344. Certification, and Approval of, Vouchers. - No money shall be disbursed unless the local budget officer certifies to the existence of appropriation that has been legally made for the purpose, the local accountant has obligated said appropriation, and the local treasurer certifies to the availability of funds for the purpose. Vouchers and payrolls shall be certified to and approved by the head of the department or office who has administrative control of the fund concerned, as to validity, propriety, and legality of the claim involved. Except in cases of disbursements involving regularly recurring administrative expenses such as payrolls for regular or permanent employees, expenses for light, water, telephone and telegraph services, remittances to government creditor agencies such as GSIS, SSS, LDP, DBP, National Printing Office, Procurement Service of the DBM and others, approval of the disbursement voucher by the local chief executive himself shall be required whenever local funds are disbursed.

connection thereto, COA Circular No. 2012-005 requires the PB to issue a Punong Barangay Certification (P BC) under oath to the depositary bank for checks issued by the barangay. In the case of PB Clemente, while he is authorized by law to approve the disbursement voucher, he is unable to perform the duties concomitant thereto in view of his disqualification to apply for fidelity bond, which is a requirement imposed upon accountable public officers pursuant to the Public Bonding Law (Sections 313-335, Revised Administrative Code of 1917). Notably, in the 26 October 2015 and 02 November 2015 letters of COA-Malabon City, the City Auditor interposed no objection to the designation of SBM Gregorio as the duly designated Finance Officer of the Barangay, in addition to the required Punong Barangay's signature considering the status of bond approved by the BTr, subject to PB Clemente's submission of a copy of the Internal Rules and Regulations adopted by the Barangay pursuant to Section 50, LGC. Notwithstanding the foregoing, we shall defer to the Department of Finance's (DOF) definitive opinion on the issue, i.e., whether the issuance of the fidelity bond may be designated by the local chief executive, in view of its mandate and administrative expertise on the matter. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary Cc DIR. MARIA LOURDES L. AGUSTIN OIC, DILG-NCR 4th Floor, Annex Building-SRA Sugar Center Compound, North Avenue Diliman, Quezon City C/DIR. EMMANUEL D. BORROMEO DILG Malabon Field Office 4th Floor, Malabon City Hall, Malabon City In cases of special or trust funds, disbursements shall be approved by the administrator of the fund. In case of temporary absence or incapacity of the department head or chief Of Office, the officer next-in-rank shall automatically perform his function and he shall be fully responsible therefor.
